edges.description: Hyperexcitable neonatal cortical networks generate multiple daily seizures beginning in the first week of life.
Synchronized hyperexcitable discharges in KCNQ2-NEO-DEE manifest predominantly as asymmetric tonic seizures.
Paroxysmal hypersynchronous network bursts alternating with voltage attenuation produce a burst-suppression or multifocal epileptiform EEG at onset.
Ictal autonomic manifestation accompanying neonatal tonic seizures.
Early network dysfunction during a critical developmental window contributes to the developmental encephalopathy.
Variant neuronal networks exhibit prolonged burst duration relative to CRISPR-corrected isogenic controls, and evoked hyperexcitability in G256W networks is rescued by retigabine.
Neonatal and postweaning motor cortical pyramidal neurons show reduced M-current conductance and increased intrinsic excitability.
Knock-in mice exhibit spontaneous EEG-confirmed generalized epileptic seizures that remit as animals age.
edges.limitations: Spontaneous generalized seizures first appear postweaning (P20-P30) rather than in the first week of life as in human KCNQ2-NEO-DEE, and neonatal burst-suppression EEG is not reported.

edges.description: Spatial learning and memory deficits persist into adulthood after spontaneous seizures subside.
edges.limitations: Adult knock-in mice exhibit spatial learning and memory deficits, whereas early postnatal neurosensory development appears grossly normal, in contrast to the moderate-to-profound global developmental impairment evident from infancy in human KCNQ2-NEO-DEE.

nodes.description: A heterozygous, usually de novo pathogenic variant in KCNQ2 (most often a missense variant in the voltage sensor or pore of the Kv7.2 subunit) alters the neuronal M channel. In NEO-DEE these variants typically act by a dominant-negative mechanism, and a minority are gain-of-function; the milder benign end of the spectrum results from simple loss-of-function or haploinsufficiency. This node captures the single concept of the initiating genetic lesion.

genetic_context.description: De novo heterozygous missense variants, typically in the pore or voltage-sensor domains. Recorded as DOMINANT_NEGATIVE, which distinguishes the encephalopathy from benign familial neonatal seizures caused by KCNQ2 haploinsufficiency: the encephalopathy alleles suppress the current of co-assembled wild-type subunits. A minority of encephalopathy alleles are instead gain-of-function and are not covered by this category.

nodes.description: Induced NGN2 excitatory glutamatergic cortical neurons differentiated from patient-derived iPSCs carrying heterozygous KCNQ2 p.Leu292_Leu293delinsProPhe, p.Gly256Trp, or p.Thr274Met variants paired with CRISPR-Cas9-corrected isogenic controls.

Heterozygous knock-in mice carrying the recurrent human KCNQ2 p.Thr274Met variant develop reduced cortical pyramidal M-current density and neuronal hyperexcitability during neonatal and postweaning stages, EEG-confirmed spontaneous generalized seizures starting around P20 that remit with age, and persistent adult spatial learning and memory deficits without gross structural brain malformations.

The M-current is a slow, non-inactivating potassium current that stabilizes the resting membrane potential and provides a brake on repetitive action-potential firing. Its reduction removes this brake, depolarizing neurons and permitting sustained firing. This node captures the single concept of the excitability-control failure.

nodes.description: KCNQ2 (Kv7.2) co-assembles with KCNQ3 (Kv7.3) to form the neuronal M channel concentrated at axon initial segments and nodes of Ranvier alongside ankyrin-G and voltage-gated sodium channels. Pathogenic variants reduce or alter M channel function; a dominant-negative subunit can suppress channels beyond simple haploinsufficiency. This node captures the single concept of the channel defect and conforms to the shared epilepsy ion-channel node.

evidence.reference_title: KCNQ2 is a nodal K+ channel.
evidence.snippet: We show here that KCNQ2 channels are functional components of axon initial segments and nodes of Ranvier, colocalizing with ankyrin-G and voltage-dependent Na+ channels throughout the CNS and PNS.
